name: FIGMA-USE
title: the MCP wizard
description: Mandatory prerequisite before any use_figma MCP call. Foundational context that prevents the most common write/read failures in Figma.
howIUse: I don't invoke it directly — it loads automatically before Figma write operations. If I'm debugging weird Figma plugin behavior, the first thing I check is whether this skill loaded.

name: FIGMA-GEN
title: the portal opener
description: Translates an app page, view, or multi-section layout from code into Figma. Triggers on 'push this to Figma', 'create in Figma from code', 'build a landing page in Figma'.
howIUse: When I want a Figma version of something I've already built in code. I point the agent at the page and say 'push this to Figma' — it lays out the screen using my design system. Saves the round-trip of recreating a design that already exists.

name: FRONTEND-DSGN
title: the architect
description: Creates distinctive, production-grade frontend interfaces with high design quality. Avoids the generic 'AI aesthetic' of identical sans-serif + flat color UI.
howIUse: Whenever I ask Claude to build a UI from scratch I want this on, otherwise the output drifts into generic. Client demos, new product pages, anything where 'good taste' matters more than 'functional'.

name: WEB-GUIDELINES
title: the inspector
description: Reviews UI code against Web Interface Guidelines — UX, accessibility, design conventions. A second-pass audit lens after you've built something.
howIUse: After I've built something I run it on the page and ask for a structured audit. Catches things I miss when I'm deep in the implementation: touch target sizes, focus states, type hierarchy, common UX mistakes.

name: ACCESSIBILITY
title: the guardian
description: Audits and improves web accessibility following WCAG 2.2. Use for a11y audits, compliance, screen reader support, keyboard navigation.
howIUse: Before shipping anything user-facing I run an a11y pass. Pairs with web-design-guidelines — that catches design issues, this catches compliance issues. Two different lenses on the same code.

name: MKT-PSYCH
title: the persuader
description: Applies psychology, mental models, and behavioral science to marketing — anchoring, social proof, scarcity, loss aversion, framing, nudge.
howIUse: When I write copy for landing pages, pricing, onboarding, or CTAs and want to ground the decision in a real principle instead of 'this feels right'. Sparring partner for goal + audience.

name: PROMPT-ENG
title: the whisperer
description: Writes, refactors, and evaluates LLM prompts. Templates, structured output schemas, evaluation rubrics, test suites.
howIUse: Every AI feature has a prompt as config. I use this to refactor flaky prompts, convert ad-hoc prompts to structured (JSON / function calling), and write evals so I know if changes actually improved things.

name: EXTRACT-DS
title: the scavenger
description: Extracts design primitives (color, type, spacing) from a public website and generates starter token files.
howIUse: Starting a new project: I point it at a reference site (competitor, design I admire, my own existing site) and get back starter tokens. Faster than from scratch, and gives a real baseline to iterate from.

name: FIND-SKILLS
title: the seeker
description: Discovers and installs agent skills when you ask 'is there a skill for X?' or 'how do I do Y?'. Surfaces things you didn't know existed.
howIUse: Before writing a custom workflow, I check if a skill already exists. Stops me reinventing things and surfaces skills I didn't know about.

name: CREATE-SKILL
title: the cursor forger
description: Authors new Cursor Agent Skills. Use when writing a SKILL.md or asking how the Cursor skill format works.
howIUse: When I'm in Cursor and notice I'm repeating the same workflow more than twice, I use this to package it as a skill.

name: WRITING-SKILLS
title: the grand forger
description: Creates, edits, and verifies skills before deployment. Best practices, examples, graph conventions, subagent-based testing.
howIUse: Most thorough of the three forger variants. I use it when the skill I'm building will be shared with others (vs. personal one-off) — includes testing and verification steps the others skip.

name: CAVEMAN
title: the token slasher
description: Ultra-compressed communication mode. Cuts token usage ~75% by speaking like caveman while keeping technical accuracy. Levels: lite, full, ultra.
howIUse: I turn it on when I want shorter, denser responses — saves tokens and reads faster. Best for iterative work where I don't need polished prose. Switch with /caveman or 'caveman mode'.

name: AI-COMPONENTS
title: the annotator
description: Generates AI-ready metadata for design system components. Analyzes structure and produces structured metadata so AI knows when and how to use each component correctly.
howIUse: When maintaining a design system that I want AI to consume intelligently. I run it on a component file and get back metadata that tells the AI when/where to use that component — critical for AI-driven UI generation against a real DS.
